---
title: "By the Numbers"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Use relative path to file from repo root (repo convention).
here::i_am("website/index.qmd")

library(here)
library(tidyverse)

# One card per state, ordered alphabetically. The accent color and flag come
# from the same sources the reports use, so the grid matches the PDFs. Each card
# links to the pre-rendered PDF (committed under website/reports/, built by
# R/render-reports.R) and downloads on click.
state_slug <- function(s) {
  s |>
    str_to_lower() |>
    str_replace_all("[^a-z]+", "_") |>
    str_remove("_$")
}

states <- read_csv(
  here("data_raw", "state_colors.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(
    slug = state_slug(state),
    pdf = str_glue("reports/{slug}-by-the-numbers.pdf"),
    flag = str_glue("flags/{slug}.svg")
  ) |>
  arrange(state)

cards <- states |>
  mutate(
    card = str_glue(
      '<a class="report-card" href="{pdf}" download style="--accent: {accent};">',
      '<span class="report-card__flag"><img src="{flag}" alt="{state} flag" loading="lazy"></span>',
      '<span class="report-card__name">{state}</span>',
      '<span class="report-card__hint">Download PDF</span>',
      "</a>"
    )
  ) |>
  pull(card)
```

A demographic and economic profile for every county, from the American
Community Survey (5-year estimates). Pick a state to download its report.

```{r}
#| label: grid
#| output: asis

# Emit the grid as a raw HTML block (```{=html}) so pandoc passes it through
# verbatim. Without the fence, pandoc reprocesses the markup and wraps the cards
# in <p> tags, which breaks the CSS grid (the cards stop being grid children).
cat("```{=html}\n")
cat('<div class="report-grid">\n')
cat(paste(cards, collapse = "\n"))
cat("\n</div>\n")
cat("```\n")
```
